newsitem.title: USA: US FCC clears Westinghouse-Infinity merger.
newsitem.headline: US FCC clears Westinghouse-Infinity merger.

text.p: The Federal Communications Commission said Thursday that it approved the merger of Infinity Broadcasting Corp and Westinghouse Electric Corp.
The FCC said it approved related conditional waivers of the broadcast multiple ownership rules as well as applications to assign certain radio stations to insulated trusts.
Also approved was Westinghouse's request for permanent one-to-a-market waivers to allow it to retain stations that it acquired in November 1995 from CBS Inc.
As a result of the merger, Westinghouse will acquire Infinity's 43 radio stations.

Westinghouse currently controls radio and telvision stations in nine of the markets where it will acquire Infinity radio stations -- New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Philadelphia, San Francisco, Detroit, Boston, Baltimore and Washington D.C.

In Boston, Baltimore and Washinton D.C., Westinghouse controls permanent radio-television combinations. The FCC said it granted temporary one-to-a-market waivers in these three markets for a period ending six months after the FCC issues its decision in the television ownership proceeding.

In the remaining six markets -- New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Philadelphia, San Francisco and Detroit -- Wesinghouse was previously granted temporary 12-month waivers for radio-television combinations that resulted from its acquisition of CBS.
The FCC granted Westinghouse's request to convert the temporary waivers to perment waivers in these six.

As a result of the Infinity merger, Westinghouse will acquire additional radio stations in each of these six markets. Conditional one-to-a-market waivers to hold the added Infinity stations in the six markets was granted for a period ending six months after the FCC issues a decision in the television ownership proceeding.

The FCC said the waivers take into consideration Westinghouse's settlement of a civil antitrust case with the Department of Justice that requires Westinghouse to divest FM radio stations WBOS, in Boston, and WMMR, in Philadelphia.

In addition, the FCC noted, Westinghouse and Infinity have filed applications to divest stations in Chicago and Dallas-Fort Worth so that the merged entity will comply with the numerical limitations of the local radio ownerhip rules.

To ensure they meet local ownership rules prior to completing the merger, even if the divestitures are not completed, Westinghouse and Infinity filed applications to assign stations in Chicago and Dallas-Forth Worth to insulated trusts. The FCC approved the trust applications for six-month periods.
In November, the FCC proposed easing local telvision station ownership rules as well as rules governing the cross-ownership of radio and TV stations.
The agency tentatively decided to waive the ban on ownership of a TV and radio station in the same market in the top 50 markets if there were at least 30 independent stations available.
Previously the FCC had waived restrictions in the top 25 markets under such circumstances.
